newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thousands oppose feared south France nuclear dump.
newsitem.headline: Thousands oppose feared south France nuclear dump.

text.p: Several thousand people protested on Friday against the possible development of a nuclear waste dump in a wine-producing tourist region of southern France.

Organisers said 5,000 people, including local mayors and winegrowers, marched through the city of Avignon with banners reading "No to the nuclear rubbish bin" and "Nuclear trash equals 180 Chernobyls." Police said 3,000 people took part.
A site at nearby Marcoule is one of three around France earmarked as a possible long-term storage dump for waste from nuclear power stations.

The state nuclear organisation Andra is to study the site's geology. If found suitable, barrels containing waste that will stay radioactive for 20,000 years would be buried 800 metres (3,000 ft) deep.
Opponents fear the scheme will undermine sales of wine from the area and put off tourists. "Nuclear cemetery, we won't have it," demonstrators chanted.

"Thirty thousand jobs are threatened in a region where the economy rests above all on the quality of life, tourism and agricultural produce," said Jerome Quilot, head of the local Cotes-du-Rhone wine-growers' group.

"French people don't do enough to counter the nuclear threat," said Ulrike, a 27-year-old German who cycled from Munich to take part in the rally. "I've come to express the support of many German people who are more aware."

Organisers explained their demands to Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou at the end of the march outside Avignon's 14th century Papal Palace. Guigou, elected to parliament from the region, was attending a local political meeting.
France, with few natural energy resources, relies on nuclear power to generate about 75 percent of its electricity and it faces a huge problem with long-term storage of nuclear waste.
